title: Cervical length ultrasound in pregnancy
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to measure the length of your cervix during pregnancy. A short cervix can be a risk for early birth.
why: Usually in the second trimester, often together with the second screening. More often if you had an early birth before or are at risk.
duration: usually 10 to 15 minutes; results right away
tell_doctor: How many weeks pregnant you are
If you had an early birth or miscarriage before
If you had surgery on your cervix
If you have cramping, discharge, or bleeding

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Usually an internal probe is used, so your bladder should be empty. Use the toilet before the scan.

prepare.title: Safety
prepare.text: The scan is safe for the baby. No special prep is needed.

steps: You undress below the waist and lie on your back
A cover with gel is put on the probe
The probe is gently placed a short way into the vagina
The doctor measures the cervix, sometimes several times
Sometimes you are asked to cough or push a little. This checks the cervix under pressure
feel: Feeling nervous is normal. Tell the doctor if it is uncomfortable
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
If your cervix is short, the doctor will discuss ways to support the pregnancy
red_flags: Contractions, bleeding from the vagina, or your water breaking: call emergency services right away

faq.q: Can an internal probe harm the baby?
faq.a: No. The probe stays near the cervix and does not touch the baby. It is the standard method.

faq.q: What if my cervix is short?
faq.a: It does not mean labor will start. There are ways to support the pregnancy. Your doctor will choose one.

reminders.text: Cervical length scan tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record. Use the toilet before the scan.
